> This feels too early for being merged. There's next to no actual content in the overlay.

Well, yes, but there's nothing wrong to have it in tests(?)
Also we only need `FriendsLayout` to be completed and then we will replace the `SocialOverlay`. And after that we can implement other layouts one by one and unlock them when ready.
The progression feels backwards. Should be going bottom-up (smallest components first) and not top-down IMO, but that might just be me.
I agree, I will implement them one-by-one, but it's easier for me to see how it will looks and feels like in the overlay itself right away rather than adjust them later after the implementation.
Will reopen after https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/8108 merge
Oh, actually it's the dashboard overlay now, will rename

I've done a basic merge of this for you, but there's plenty of further changes required which I'm going to leave to you:

- Because of the way you've structured these "Layouts" (please use the term "Display" going forward) they are not online components, and do not correctly handle API state changes. You need to add this functionality.
- Keep in mind that this applies to all your "layout" classes. At which point if you are following along you'd realise it's basically trying to be a FullscreenOverlay without being one. Maybe this is okay, but something to keep in mind.
- There's a loading spinner at dashboard. But then you also have on in the friend display. I'd recommend removing the spinner from the dashboard.
- The loading spinner on friends only displays when going from nothing to something. seems a bit wrong? Is this due to layout issues?
I accidentally broke this branch... Will apply requested changes in the new one.
how?
I had a local outdated commit and accidentally pushed it. So some magic happened and now I can't see your latest changes to this branch even after full branch re-pull
Nevermind, I figured this out. Only with force-push, sorry

> * Because of the way you've structured these "Layouts" they are not online components, and do not correctly handle API state changes. You need to add this functionality.

This logic handled by the overlay itself (https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/8051/files#diff-2ba431d9d74d076aa7dc226deb3b12a6R81, https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/8051/files#diff-2ba431d9d74d076aa7dc226deb3b12a6R97). Is it bad?

Actually, my statement above is stupid, because now we have half of online logic in the overlay and half in the display. So the question is: is it better to handle all the online logic by the overlay and make displays full-offline (I mean, like in rankings, when all the requests are handled by the overlay and displays just accept the data) or the overlay should be only just a "container which only selects the needed display" and everything online will be handled by displays?

(This might veer a little general, but it's beginning to be a general discussion, so I suppose it's not entirely out of place?)

I've had this idea for an overarching structure of overlays that could probably be best explained with the following diagram:

![Untitled Diagram(8)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/77357911-3a842380-6d49-11ea-857d-7897d34e7544.png)

Easier said than done to achieve most likely, but I think this is a pattern that could end up working for us.

Refactored. Now all the online logic is handled in the overlay itself. (Grabbed some logic from the rankings with small improvements, in the future these overlays should share their logic). Feels way better and have more sense now!
@EVAST9919 requires conflict resolution
Resolved
@EVAST9919 i'm not 100% sure what i'm looking at here. did you intend to structure things how @bdach asked for?

To reiterate the general direction this should be moving towards:

- `DashboardOverlay` should not be doing any online logic
- `FriendDisplay` should inherit a new class `OverlayView` which implements basic `IOnlineComponent` (copy paste from `FullscreenOverlay` really)

This differs slightly from @bdach's diagram as it combines the view and controller, but I think this is enough for us for now (and quite a common practice).

And just to clarify, `FullscreenOverlay` is still fine to be an `IOnlineComponent`. It is still fine to handle requests when it's an overlay with *one* scope. But Dashboard has many scopes which need to be separated from each other else we are going to become huge class-wise.
